# Module 00: Your Relationship to the Model

<!-- Generated by `aicg org render-orientation` from config/stances.json and the org manifests. Edit those, not this file. -->

> **Role:** AI Enablement Lead · **Org:** AI Workforce Curriculum · **Level:** L45

Every role in the AI Career Curriculum works on the same thing, a model, from a different side. Before the technical modules, this one tells you which side is yours, what you own there, and who you depend on.

## Where you stand

You **work alongside** the model: you direct it, check its output, and redesign your own work around it.

To you the model is a colleague with uneven skills: fast, tireless, often right, sometimes confidently wrong. You don't build or run it. You decide what to hand it, how to brief it, how to verify what comes back, and which parts of the job stay yours. Your craft is the judgment around the model, not the model itself.

## The six relationships

| Org | Relationship to the model |
|-----|---------------------------|
| [AI Workforce](https://github.com/ai-workforce-curriculum) *(you are here)* | You **work alongside** the model: you direct it, check its output, and redesign your own work around it. |
| [AI Startup](https://github.com/ai-startup-curriculum) | You **build a company around** the model: you decide what it's for and who pays for it. |
| [AI Governance](https://github.com/ai-governance-curriculum) | You **govern and assure** the model: you decide whether a use is acceptable and prove it stays that way. |
| [AI Engineering](https://github.com/ai-engineering-curriculum) | You **build with** the model: you turn it into products and agents people use. |
| [ML Engineering](https://github.com/ml-engineering-curriculum) | You **build and train** the model: you decide what it learns. |
| [AI Infrastructure](https://github.com/AI-Infra-Curriculum) | You **run** the model: you keep it available, fast, and affordable. |

## What you own

- Which tasks to delegate to models and agents, and which to keep
- Briefing: the context, constraints, and examples that get usable output
- Verification: reviewing, testing, and fact-checking what the model produces
- Workflows and team habits that make AI-assisted work repeatable and safe
- Accountability for the result, whoever (or whatever) drafted it

**What you don't own:** The model, the tools built on it, or the policy that governs them. You're their most demanding user: you report where they fail real work and push for the fixes.

Each row is a sibling org: what you hand them, what they hand you, and the role there closest to your level, the person you're most likely to work with.

| AI Infrastructure | Real usage patterns and pain points (latency, limits, outages) from people whose day depends on the tools | Reliable, fast, well-documented AI tools with clear limits, so a working day doesn't stall on an outage or a rate limit | [AI Infrastructure Architect](https://github.com/AI-Infra-Curriculum/ai-infra-architect-learning) |

## Your ladder

- **Before this role:** [AI-Augmented Team Manager](https://github.com/ai-workforce-curriculum/ai-augmented-team-manager-learning)
- **After this role:** this is the top of this ladder. Growth from here usually means moving across to a sibling org's senior roles.

## Scenario: One model upgrade, six orgs

Your vendor ships a new model version and deprecates the one in production in 90 days. Nobody owns this end to end. Here is how the work splits across the six orgs:

1. **AI Workforce:** **Re-checks the everyday workflows built on the old model (prompts, review habits, team playbooks), spots where output quality shifted, and updates the guidance people actually follow.** ← your part
2. **AI Startup:** Decides whether the upgrade is worth it now: cost, customer commitments, roadmap. Tells customers what changes and when.
3. **AI Governance:** Re-runs risk and safety evaluations on the new version, updates the model inventory and documentation, and signs off (or blocks) the release.
4. **AI Engineering:** Re-runs product evals, re-tunes prompts and tool definitions that regressed, and rolls the new model out behind a flag with a rollback path.
5. **ML Engineering:** Re-validates any fine-tunes, distillations, or in-house models that depended on the old version, and benchmarks the new one on the team's own data.
6. **AI Infrastructure:** Stands up serving for the new version, capacity-plans GPUs or rate limits, shifts traffic gradually, and watches latency, error, and cost dashboards.

If any one of these is skipped, the upgrade fails in a way the others can't see from where they sit. Knowing which line is yours, and who owns the lines next to it, is the point of this module.
